title: Company-wide policies and processes: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Ava Nguyen
body:
Purpose
This consolidated document defines Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and repeatable processes for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended to be the single source of truth for employees and teams when executing routine operational tasks or escalating exceptions.

Scope and ownership
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who access company systems or manage company data.
- Primary owners: People Ops (policy custodians), Security (controls, RBAC), Finance & Legal (procurement, vendor contracts), Eng Platform & SRE (change procedures, infra access).

Quick links
- Access request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request
- Change request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-request
- Vendor assessment checklist: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/vendor-assessment
- Travel & expense form: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/travel-expense

1) Access and permissions
Overview:
- Principle: least privilege by default; role-based access control (RBAC) where supported; temporary elevated access for approved tasks. All access must be auditable.
Roles and responsibilities:
- People Ops: onboarding/offboarding coordination and identity lifecycle policies.
- Security: approves privileged roles, owns break-glass process, maintains access review schedule.
- Team owners (service/product managers): approve access to project-level resources.
Standard access process (normal requests):
1. User submits Access Request using the Access Request template with justification and expiration date.
2. Request routed to team owner for approval (target SLA: 3 business days).
3. Security performs entitlement check for privileged roles and approves or requests clarifications.
4. Provisioning completed by the relevant system owner or automated identity provider (IdP) workflow.
Emergency / break-glass access:
- Emergency access can be granted via the break-glass process: requester opens an incident channel and submits an emergency access request. Approvals: Security on-call + service owner. Emergency access must be time-limited to max 12 hours and is mandatory to log actions.
Access reviews and recertification:
- Quarterly access review for all privileged roles; annual certification for non-privileged group memberships. Team owners must confirm or revoke access via the access review portal.
Key controls and technical requirements:
- MFA enforced for all accounts.
- Idle session timeout: 30 minutes for console access.
- Service accounts must be managed and rotated every 90 days or use short-lived credentials.

2) Change management
Overview:
- Purpose: ensure safe, auditable, low-risk changes to production and shared infrastructure while enabling rapid delivery. Changes are categorized and approved according to risk.
Change categories:
- Standard: pre-authorized low-risk changes (e.g., routine config updates) that follow a documented runbook.
- Normal: scheduled changes requiring approval via the Change Request template and CAB review for medium risk.
- Emergency: unplanned work to restore service; post-facto CAB review required.
Process for normal changes (summary):
1. Submit Change Request with scope, rollback plan, test plan, impact analysis, and owner.
2. Requestor obtains team owner sign-off and attaches test evidence.
3. CAB review window (weekly) assesses risk and approval.
4. Schedule change in approved deployment window (default: Tue-Thu 09:00-17:00 PT).
5. Execute, monitor, and document result.
6. Post-change review and close.
Rollback and canary/gradual rollout guidance:
- All production changes must have a clear rollback plan and defined success criteria. Use canary deployments and 10-50% progressive rollouts for changes that affect customer-facing latency or correctness.
Automation and CI/CD gates:
- Pipeline gates must run integration tests, canary checks, and automated rollback triggers. Manual gates are required for changes classified as high risk.
Change windows and maintenance notices:
- Maintenance windows published at /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts. Notifications to customers and internal teams are required for changes with expected impact >5 minutes.

3) Data management and governance
Data classification:
- Confidential: PII, customer secrets, payment data, and any regulated data.
- Internal: company-internal but not customer-sensitive.
- Public: information cleared for public release.
Handling and controls:
- Encryption: at-rest and in-transit encryption required for Confidential data (AES-256 / TLS1.2+).
- Data minimization: collect and store the minimum data required for the business purpose.
- Access: data access requests follow the Access Request process and require business justification.
Retention and deletion:
- Standard retention periods: logs (90 days), product telemetry (1 year), backups (90 days unless otherwise specified), customer support data (as per contract). Any deviation must be approved by Security and Legal.
Backups and recovery:
- Critical systems must have automated backups with documented RTO/RPO. Restore runbooks must be tested annually.
Data residency and transfer:
- Data residency requirements (customer-imposed or regulatory) must be enforced via region-specific deployments. Cross-border transfers require Legal review.
Data breach and incident reporting:
- Security incident process in /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security must be followed. Any confirmed data exposure must be reported to Legal within 24 hours.

4) Procurement and expenses
Procurement thresholds and approvals matrix:
- <= $5,000: Department head approval.
- $5,001 - $50,000: Finance approval + Department head.
- > $50,000: Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor.
Procurement process steps:
1. Requester completes a Purchase Request with justification, ETA, and budget code.
2. Department head reviews and approves.
3. Finance validates budget and issues PO if required.
4. Legal reviews contracts for commitments > $10,000 or where liability/SLAs are material.
5. Vendor onboarding only after Security and Legal clearance.
Expense reimbursement rules:
- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days using the Travel & Expense template with receipts. Card reconciliation must occur monthly. Non-compliant submissions may be denied.
Corporate card usage:
- Cardholders must follow the Corporate Card Policy (link in templates). Card limits and approvers are managed by Finance.

5) Vendor management
Vendor risk tiers:
- Low: commodity services with no access to customer or confidential data.
- Medium: vendors with limited access to internal systems or metadata.
- High: vendors with access to Confidential data, production systems, or administrative privileges. High-risk vendors require an extended security assessment.
Vendor onboarding checklist (required):
- Business justification and owner.
- Contract reviewed and signed by Legal.
- Security assessment completed (questionnaire + evidence).
- Data access and retention terms documented.
- Registrar of vendor credentials and points of contact maintained by Procurement.
Vendor reviews and KPIs:
- Annual performance and security review for medium/high vendors. Include uptime, SLO adherence, and security posture.
Termination and offboarding:
- Revoke all vendor access immediately upon contract termination and confirm data retention/deletion per contract terms.

6) Travel policy (business travel)
Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked through the company travel portal or approved travel agent. Domestic travel requires manager approval; international travel requires People Ops and manager approval.
Per diems and allowable expenses:
- Per diem rates follow the company table (link in templates). Business meals and transportation are reimbursable with receipts. Alcohol allowed only when accompanied by a business purpose and manager approval.
Expense submission and timelines:
- Submit expenses within 30 days of trip end. Late submissions require manager approval and may be denied.
Duty of care and emergency contact:
- Travelers must share itinerary with People Ops. For emergencies, contact People Ops on-call number or security@redwood.com.

7) Internal templates and artifacts
Available templates (canonical):
- Access Request (access-request)
- Change Request (change-request)
- Vendor Assessment (vendor-assessment)
- Travel & Expense Form (travel-expense)
- Procurement / PO Request (purchase-request)
- Incident RCA template (incident-rca)
How to use templates:
- Templates are hosted under /confluence/policies-and-process/templates. Clone and complete the template in the requester's team space and attach necessary evidence.

Exceptions and escalation
- Any exception to policy must be submitted via the Exceptions Request form and include a compensating controls plan. Exceptions are reviewed by the Risk & Exceptions board monthly.
- If an urgent policy conflict arises (security, legal, or financial exposure), escalate immediately to the relevant on-call team and notify People Ops.

Governance and review cadence
- Policy owners must review and update this document annually or after any significant regulatory change.
- People Ops maintains a policy changelog and publishes changes via company-wide announcement.

Appendices
A. Approval matrix (summary)
- Access approvals: Team owner -> Security (privileged) -> People Ops provisioning.
- Procurement approvals: Dept head -> Finance -> Legal -> Exec sponsor (for large spend).

B. Contact list
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security (access & incident): security@redwood.com
- Finance (procurement & cards): finance@redwood.com
- Legal (contracts): legal@redwood.com

C. Change window calendar
- Published at /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/change-calendar

D. How to request an exception
1. Complete Exceptions Request template with business justification, duration, and compensating controls.
2. Submit to Risk & Exceptions board for review (target SLA: 10 business days).
3. Implement compensating controls while exception is active and document closure when resolved.

If you have questions about how these policies apply to a specific situation, contact People Ops or the relevant owner listed above.
